'''''Phalaris caroliniana''''' is a species of [[Poaceae|grass]] known as '''Carolina canarygrass''' and '''maygrass'''.

== Background ==
It is native to the southern United States,<ref name=usda>[https://plants.sc.egov.usda.gov/plant-profile/PHCA6 USDA Plants Profile: Phalaris caroliniana]</ref> and it can be found as a [[introduced species|naturalized species]] along the west coast of the United States,<ref>{{cite web |title=''Phalaris caroliniana'' |url=https://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-calrecnum=6421 |website=www.calflora.org |publisher=Calflora |accessdate=1 October 2019}}</ref> as well as northern Mexico and parts of Europe and Australia.{{citation needed|date=September 2019}} It is most often found in moist to wet habitats, such as marshy meadows, and it can thrive in disturbed areas. It is an annual grass reaching a maximum height between {{cvt|1 and 1.5|m|ft}}. The hairy [[inflorescence]] is roughly oval in shape and up to {{cvt|7|cm}} long by {{cvt|2|cm}} wide.

This grass probably made up part of the [[Eastern Agricultural Complex]] of plants cultivated by pre-Columbian [[Native Americans in the United States]]. Its grains have been identified in [[archaeological site]]s from [[Texas]] to [[Indiana]] to [[Alabama]] which may be four millennia old.<ref>{{cite web |author-surname=Roberts |author-given=Katherine M. |url=http://artsci.wustl.edu/~gjfritz/Phalaris_caroliniana_Walter.html |title=Phalaris caroliniana |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100706032014/http://artsci.wustl.edu/~gjfritz/Phalaris_caroliniana_Walter.html |archive-date=2010-07-06 |work=Laboratory Guide To Archaeological Plant Remains From Eastern North America |publisher=[[Washington University in St. Louis]] |url-status=dead}}</ref> Laboratory analysis of the grass seed indicates that it is quite nutritious, with a good amount of vitamins and minerals.<ref>Crites, G. D. & R. D. Terry. (1984).  Nutritive value of maygrass, ''Phalaris caroliniana''. ''Economic Botany''  38:1 114-20.</ref>
